headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared filesystem or MCP bridge is documented, but Superset’s allowlisted egress and Whisper’s audio-file inputs create limited indirect leakage and workflow-conflict possibilities.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Superset has no documented shared communication channel to Whisper, and Whisper exposes only audio-file input with no clipboard, MCP, or filesystem write path. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between Superset and Whisper, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe Superset outputs into Whisper as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Superset can make allowlisted network egress, while Whisper processes audio files and has no filesystem read/write or network egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace, so leakage is limited unless operators manually move sensitive audio or transcripts between them.
conditions: IF operators place sensitive audio or transcripts into both tools’ workflows, data can be exposed across the pair.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive audio out of Superset workflows.
Store Whisper inputs and outputs in separate directories.
Disable any manual export of transcripts into Superset unless reviewed.
requires-engineering: add access controls if a shared workspace is needed.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Superset’s documented surface is API access and allowlisted egress; Whisper has no filesystem write, shell, subprocess, git, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource, so a capability conflict is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF Superset is deployed with additional write access not shown in the profile, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Avoid granting Superset write access to shared state.
Document any future shared mutable resource before pairing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Superset can consume API-backed analytics outputs, but Whisper is a sequence-to-sequence model with no downstream action authority. The pair could still propagate mistaken transcripts or summaries if an operator treats Whisper output as authoritative, yet no automatic action chain is documented.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are fed into Superset dashboards or reports without review, errors can cascade.
IF an operator automates decisions from Whisper output, impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review of Whisper output before ingestion.
Label Whisper output as unverified text.
Use a validation step before any Superset report is published.
requires-engineering: add automated transcript confidence checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Superset’s profile shows no touched data classes or special compliance claims, while Whisper explicitly touches audio and speech. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to handling audio content carefully rather than a clear policy breach.
conditions: IF audio files contain regulated content and are routed through an unapproved workflow, compliance review is required.
IF future deployment assigns different retention policies to Superset and Whisper, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated audio into Superset.
Align retention settings for transcripts and reports.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls if regulated data is used.
